summary.text: The mesopelagic or twilight zone is the ocean layer from about 200 to 1,000 m deep, starting where only 1% of light reaches and ending where no light remains.
It plays a key role in the ocean's biological pump: an estimated 90% of the organic carbon sinking into it from the sunlit layer is respired there.
Cut off from the air and busy breaking down sinking organic matter, it often develops a zone of minimum oxygen.

facts.label: Sound channel
facts.value: SOFAR channel at its base, about 600–1,200 m

items.prompt: Organic carbon sinks out of the sunlit layer into the twilight zone below. Roughly how much of it is respired there?

options.label: About 10%
About 30%
About 90%
About 50%

items.explain: An estimated 90% of the particulate organic carbon exported from the sunlit zone is respired in the mesopelagic.

items.prompt: A shipwreck survivor drops a small charge timed to explode in the SOFAR channel. Why can far-off listening stations pick it up?

options.label: The blast pushes a large wave onto the surface
Sound is trapped in that layer and travels far
The flash of light is seen from great distances
The charge sends a radio signal to the stations

items.explain: In the SOFAR channel, sound waves bend back within the layer and travel long distances, so stations can locate the raft.

items.prompt: Why does the twilight zone so often run low on oxygen?

options.label: Its fish breathe faster than fish at the surface
Its plants take in oxygen instead of releasing it
Its cold water cannot hold any dissolved gas
Decay uses oxygen up and no air reaches it

items.explain: Respiration of sinking organic matter consumes oxygen, and stratification keeps the zone out of direct contact with the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Compared with the sunlit water just above it, how rich in nutrients is the twilight zone usually?

options.label: Richer, since sinking matter is broken down there
Poorer, since sunlight drives nutrients upward
The same, since the water mixes freely
Empty, since nothing reaches that depth

items.explain: Respiration and remineralization of sinking organic particles make the mesopelagic generally nutrient-rich, while the sunlit layer is often nutrient-limited.

items.prompt: Some animals swim daily between the sunlit layer and the twilight zone. What effect does this have on organic matter?

options.label: It lifts organic matter up to the surface
It has no effect on organic matter at all
It carries organic matter down to the deep
It turns organic matter straight into oxygen

items.explain: Diel vertical migration actively transports particulate organic matter to the deep.

items.prompt: Bristlemouths and bioluminescent jellyfish thrive in the twilight zone. What condition are they adapted to?

options.label: Bright, steady sunshine
Low light
Fresh water
Air exposure at low tide

items.explain: The zone's diverse community is adapted to living in a low-light environment.
